Single Nucleotide Polymorphisms Understanding
monogenic disorders such as those described above helps lay 
the groundwork for comprehending the complexities of poly-
genic diseases such as obesity, diabetes, cancer, and cardio-
vascular disease.22 Th e study of gene-nutrient interactions that
are dependent upon gene variance (nutrigenetics) is focused
primarily on single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs, pro-
nounced “snips”).23 SNPs are deﬁ ned as those genetic variants
or polymorphisms in which a single nucleotide has been ex-
